For this exercise, you should create the R code needed to make a basic map of the locations of homicides in the Retiro neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 2023.

## Before you start

Complete Chapters 1–2 of [_Learn Crime Mapping with R_](https://books.lesscrime.info/learncrimemapping/).

In this exercise you will practise downloading and reading data, converting coordinates into a spatial object, and creating a point map. The coordinate-system codes needed for this dataset are supplied below.


### What your map should show

Your map should show the locations of individual incidents between 1 January and 31 December 2023, inclusive. You can download the data from:

```
https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/retiro_homicides.csv
```

The [dataset documentation](https://pkgs.lesscrime.info/crimemappingdata/reference/retiro_homicides.html) describes the columns and source. Although the column names are in Spanish, the file uses commas to separate values, so read it with `read_csv()` rather than `read_csv2()`.

This dataset uses the WGS84 coordinate reference system, which has the EPSG code EPSG:4326. Before creating the map you should transform the dataset to use the POSGAR 2007 / Argentina 6 coordinate system (EPSG:5348).


### Checklist for this exercise

You can use this checklist to make sure you have done everything required for this exercise.


#### The map

- The map shows the locations of individual incidents in 2023.
- The map includes a background map so viewers can identify the locations.
- The points use a colour that stands out from the background.


#### The code

- There is no temporary code – e.g. `head()`, `excel_sheets()`, `install.packages()`, etc. – in your script file.
- The code loads the necessary packages _at the start of the script_ in a single call to the `pacman::p_load()` function.
- The code uses `request()` and `req_perform()` to download the data to a local file in the `data/raw` folder.
- The code uses `here()` to specify file paths within your workspace.
- The code loads the downloaded local file into R.
- The code converts the data to a simple features (SF) object using EPSG:4326.
- The code transforms the dataset to use a local coordinate reference system.
- The script contains all the code needed to produce the map.


### Check your answer

After attempting the task, you can read this [specimen answer and explanation](retiro_homicides_answer.qmd) to get an idea of what a potential solution looks like.
